rationale.conceptual: The task applies standard first-principles methods (DFT, CI-NEB, capacity/voltage formulas) in a routine manner, using open-source code and well-documented pseudopotentials. It requires understanding of DFT setup and battery metrics but no novel theory or complex algorithm implementation.
rationale.execution: The pipeline involves multiple sequential stages: unit cell relaxation, bulk metal calculations, supercell construction, iterative adsorption studies, and NEB diffusion barrier calculations. Dependency management between DFT runs and tool orchestration (Quantum ESPRESSO + ASE + pseudopotential fetching) adds moderate engineering complexity.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires standard DFT calculations (geometry optimization, adsorption energies, CI-NEB) on a small monolayer system, applying well-established electrochemical formulas. The method is not novel; the workflow is a multi-step pipeline but with typical computational materials science tools. Resources are modest (CPU, small cell).

compute_estimate.reasoning: Small system (<40 atoms) plane-wave DFT calculations on CPU; typical memory ~4 GB per run; input data is trivial (crystal structures only).
